messages:
sam (support): FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — they say the assistant answers changed meaningfully after last night's rollout. They included a tiny repro showing different completions for the same chat input. They think a tokenizer change + chat template tweak might be the culprit. Pasting their minimal repro below.

sam (support): Customer repro (POST to /v1/chat/completions):
```json
{
  "model": "open-rl-medium",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant. Provide direct facts."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "List three reasons why battery life on older phones is worse than new ones."}
  ]
}
```

sam (support): Expected (pre-rollout) snippet: 
```
1) battery chemistry ages -> capacity loss
2) background app management gets worse over time
3) newer power-saving hardware/firmware not present
```

sam (support): Observed (post-rollout) snippet: 
```
1) battery chemistry ages -> lower capacity
2) apps use more power (see settings)
3) homescreen widgets cause wakelocks
```

sam (support): Customer notes that language shifted to device-specific UI suggestions (widgets, settings) that used to be absent. They only changed the chat template (trimmed system prompt) and applied tokenizer patch to fix token counts in analytics.

maya (eng): Thanks, looking. Can you confirm model variant and exact deploy id? Also did customer send raw tokenization diffs?

sam (support): Variant reported: open-rl-medium:v3. Deploy bot reported last night: `deploy-bot: rollout completed: commit ae3f7c3 -> models/open-rl-medium:v3` (customer said after ~22:30 UTC). Customer attached token diffs but I trimmed PII.

deploy-bot: rollout comment: Applied chat-template normalizations and tokenizer "boundary-fix" patch to reduce spurious tokens in system messages.

eli (runtime): If the system prompt changed (even trim) it can shift attention and prefix tokens — that often nudges generation. Tokenizer boundary changes could also merge/separate tokens leading to different top-p sampling. We should repro locally.

maya (eng): Repro steps I will try: 1) checkout commit ae3f7c3 2) run local serving with same model config 3) run both tokenizers (old/new) on the system+user concat and dump token ids 4) run 5 seeds with same temperature and compare completions.

nina (product): Customer impact: they use exact-answer heuristics in downstream parsers, so wording change breaks matching. They want either rollback or a targeted patch to keep system prompt semantics.

eli (runtime): Quick triage finding: ran tokenizer diff on the customer's system+user string. Old tokenizer tokenization: `[..., 124, 905, 33]` New tokenizer: `[..., 124, 905, 33, 1]` — an extra leading token near the system/user boundary. That can shift decoding.

maya (eng): OK that explains drift. Two options: revert tokenizer boundary-fix (risky) or introduce a deterministic sentinel token in chat template to anchor generation so downstream wording is stable. We should also add an A/B rollout to verify.

sam (support): Customer asks for a patch that preserves wording. Can we offer a temporary workaround they can apply client-side?

eli (runtime): Workaround: prepend an explicit separator token in the user message (e.g., "---") or add a short anchor sentence to the system prompt like: "Answer in three numbered points without UI suggestions." That is brittle but fast.

maya (eng): I'll prepare an internal canary that reverts only the tokenizer boundary change for open-rl-medium and run a comparison job. If results match pre-rollout outputs within threshold we can expand rollback.

nina (product): Also log this as a product regression: change in system prompt/tokenization caused semantic shift. Need better evals for chat-template changes.

sam (support): Customer prefers config change from our side (since they have many end users). Can we give ETA for rollback?

maya (eng): ETA: initial canary results in 2 hours, if green we can rollback within the day.

eli (runtime): Repro notes for internal run (pasting command):
```bash
# reproduce with seed and deterministic sampling
curl -s -X POST https://internal-run/api/chat -d '{"model":"open-rl-medium:v3","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise assistant. Provide direct facts."},{"role":"user","content":"List three reasons why battery life on older phones is worse than new ones."}],"temperature":0.3,"seed":42}' | jq .choices[0].message.content
```

maya (eng): Also dumping KV cache traces and token-attribution for the first 32 tokens to diagnose where the shift starts.

sam (support): I'll update AcmeCorp: offer the temporary anchor sentence and say we're testing rollback. Also ask for any cached prompts they send (they use a templating layer).

nina (product): Action items: 1) maya run canary; 2) eli produce token diffs and influence curves; 3) sam coordinate customer comms and gather more examples; 4) product to add guardrail for chat-template changes.

sam (support): Thanks team. Customer appreciates quick response, flagged as P1 for downstream parsing break. :white_check_mark:
